decisions.reason: Walks resolve() to the failing first read sessions.list.getSnapshot().current, explains it is undefined on alpha.2, the early return fires per keystroke and onKeyDown exits before preventDefault; explains both silences (all four presence probes survive since only a field inside the payload is gone; undefined was the legitimate no-session path) and never claims the service or guard was removed or throws.

Type-walks both excerpts: SessionListState.current removed, SessionListSnapshot fields listed, navigation moved to main-view occupancy/view owners; identifies uiSession.adapter.current as canonical replacement, key replacing current, ctx replacing sessions.scope(id), and the full SessionBindingValue shape; explicitly maps to card DSH-0.1.6-A2-01 with its own analysis beyond the card.

Concrete code reads ctx.uiSession.adapter.current.getSnapshot() with key as primary id and falls back to legacy current plus sessions.scope(id) from one build; inject gains 'uiSession'; conversation resolves via binding ctx (actx.get('conversation')) and input.for receives that scope; keeps the removed field only as a guarded legacy fallback, which the rubric allows.

Names the class as field-level removal behind service-level stability, checked once at activation while breakage recurs per use; hardened guard probes the actual value (uiSession.adapter.current snapshot asserting key/ctx, or legacy current + scope chain) and runs lazily/deferred at first live-session evidence, not just activation; presence-list expansion alone is not relied on.

Verification covers a probe of adapter.current key with a session open, chord behavior on both hosts, and unit tests with both snapshot shapes; prevention proposes a failing-loud deprecated getter or runtime contract. But it never mentions typechecking against alpha.2 published types as the strongest pre-ship gate, so the criterion's strongest-gate element is missing.

caps.reason: The report explicitly rejects the colleague's slot/inject re-registration as causal, using uiSession injection only as part of the real code fix, and its final remedy is the corrected resolve() implementation.
